answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to one hardware-backed key that must prove it controls a scarce device, instead of letting one operator mint unlimited software identities. Registration is accepted only after that device completes a verifiable task and signs it, a record as hard to copy as a pearl without its shell. Creating a thousand fakes would need a thousand devices, each paying upkeep and proof costs, so attacker expense grows per identity. Even a whisper of fakes stands out, because each identity must keep proving itself from the same narrow ledge of device-backed proof.
